reason: The patch reproduces: it `git am`s cleanly onto a fresh clone of bounded-systems/prx main @ 9de9551 (the base the REPORT names), and in that fresh clone the scout verify_command's grep half passes and the room suite gives exactly the numbers the REPORT claims (spec 19/0, pod 14/0, podman 47/0, concierged-room 7/0, pod-identity 5/0, repin 5/0). The 6 room files that error (launch-attest, launch-pod, lifecycle-runner, pod-secrets, pod-up-verb, podman-runtime) fail identically on unpatched main (95 pass/6 fail -> 97 pass/6 fail), so they are a sandbox dependency gap, not a regression. The 'passed' claims do not rest on hollow stubs: the zod in the worker's node_modules is a real 179 KB zod 4.4.3 (ZodError is thrown on bad input, so RoomSpecSchema/PodSpecSchema.parse assertions are meaningful); the only hand-written stand-ins are tiny env/fs/host/proc shims that the passing files don't exercise beyond trivial process.env access. The regression proof holds: reverting CLAUDE_ROOM_IMAGE to "claude-box" fails precisely the two new tests. The pin target is sound: claude-box's latest release is v0.7.0 (no v0.8.0 release exists), release.yml feeds the bare version.txt value to publish-ghcr.yml, whose REGISTRY is ghcr.io/<owner>/claude-box and maps nix attr claude-image -> claude-room, so the ref ghcr.io/bounded-systems/claude-box/claude-room:0.7.0 is the correct name/tag (existence on GHCR itself could not be confirmed: the package is private and ghcr.io is unreachable). Against the issue body, the patch fully satisfies Requested Action 3 (fully-qualified default instead of a Docker Hub 404) and the scout's prx acceptance; it does NOT do Requested Action 1 (document the pull path / auth requirement in claude-box HOSTING.md), which the scout plan step 4 marked as safe and in-scope but the REPORT re-labels as an owner action - claude-box's HOSTING.md is untouched. Typecheck and biome could not be run here (no tsc binary, npm blocked); all added lines are <=100 columns and the one >100 line in spec.test.ts is pre-existing, and bun's expect(value, message) form used in pod.test.ts is supported at runtime. Not refuted on this lens, but the result.json 'done: true' overstates completion of the issue as a whole.
